name: Budapest
operatingHours: Metro (M1-M4) runs ~4:30 AM-~11:10 PM daily, every 2-6 min by day and ~8-10 min late. No all-night metro; night buses (900-series) and trams run every ~10-30 min between ~11 PM and ~4:30 AM.
fareInfo: BKK single ticket ~HUF 500 (2026; ~HUF 700 from the driver, one metro line or one trip without transfers). Travel cards: 24 h ~HUF 2,750, 72 h ~HUF 5,750. Buy in the BudapestGO app, ticket machines or by contactless card on the Pay&GO readers; validate paper tickets before boarding. The 100E airport express needs a flat airport ticket (~HUF 2,500).

sights.name: Hungarian Parliament Building
sights.note: The neo-Gothic riverside parliament, visited on timed guided tours that include the Holy Crown of Hungary and the grand staircase.
sights.hours: Guided tours daily ~8 AM-4 PM (hours vary on session days)

sights.name: Fisherman's Bastion
sights.note: Fairytale neo-Romanesque terraces and turrets on Castle Hill with the best sweeping view of the Danube and Pest.
sights.hours: Terraces open 24 h; upper towers ticketed ~9 AM-7 PM (to 8 PM in summer)

sights.name: Shoes on the Danube Bank
sights.note: A moving memorial of 60 iron shoes on the embankment, remembering Jews shot into the river in 1944-45.

sights.name: St. Stephen's Basilica
sights.note: Hungary's largest church, with an interior of gold and marble and a panoramic dome walkway.
sights.hours: Mon-Fri ~9 AM-5 PM, Sat ~9 AM-1 PM, Sun afternoon; dome ~10 AM-5 PM

sights.name: Buda Castle
sights.note: The royal palace crowning Castle Hill, now home to the National Gallery and Budapest History Museum; the courtyards and terraces are free.
sights.hours: Grounds open 24 h; museums Tue-Sun 10 AM-6 PM, closed Mon

sights.name: Hospital in the Rock Nuclear Bunker Museum
sights.note: A Cold War hospital and fallout shelter dug into Castle Hill, visited by guided tour with waxwork wards.
sights.hours: Daily ~10 AM-7 PM, tours on the hour

sights.name: Matthias Church
sights.note: The Gothic coronation church with colourful Zsolnay roof tiles and a richly painted interior.
sights.hours: Mon-Fri ~9 AM-5 PM, Sat ~9 AM-1 PM, Sun ~1-5 PM

sights.name: Széchenyi Chain Bridge
sights.note: The first permanent bridge across the Danube, guarded by stone lions; at its best at night when lit.

sights.name: Hungarian State Opera House
sights.note: A neo-Renaissance opera house with a gilded auditorium, seen on guided tours or an evening performance.
sights.hours: Guided tours daily (times vary); box office ~11 AM-evening

sights.name: House of Terror Museum
sights.note: The former secret-police headquarters on Andrássy út, documenting fascist and communist rule through eerie exhibits.

sights.name: Margaret Island
sights.note: A car-free park island with rose gardens, a musical fountain, running track and thermal spa.

sights.name: Heroes' Square
sights.note: The monumental plaza with statues of Hungary's founding chieftains and kings, gateway to City Park.

sights.name: Vajdahunyad Castle
sights.note: A park folly that copies famous Hungarian buildings across the centuries, set around a boating lake.
sights.hours: Grounds open 24 h; Agricultural Museum Tue-Sun ~10 AM-5 PM

sights.name: Gellért Hill & Citadella
sights.note: A steep hill south of the castle with the Liberty Statue and the best free panorama of the whole city.

sights.name: Central Market Hall
sights.note: The grand iron-and-glass market hall for paprika, sausages, produce and lángos snacks on the upper floor.
sights.hours: Mon 6 AM-5 PM, Tue-Fri 6 AM-6 PM, Sat 6 AM-3 PM, closed Sun

sights.name: Great Synagogue (Dohány Street)
sights.note: Europe's largest synagogue, in Moorish style, with a museum, memorial garden and Holocaust memorial.
sights.hours: Sun-Thu ~10 AM-5:30 PM, Fri ~10 AM-3 PM (Oct), closed Sat

sights.name: Gozsdu Udvar
sights.note: A chain of seven connected courtyards in the old Jewish Quarter, now a lively strip of ruin bars and restaurants.

railStations.name: Budapest Keleti
railStations.note: The Eastern station: trains to Vienna, Prague (EuroCity), Bratislava, Munich/Salzburg and Bucharest/Vienna Railjets, plus domestic lines. Metro M2 and M4 stop right at the door.
railStations.hours: Station open ~4 AM-~midnight; trains to individual timetables; M2/M4 ~4:30 AM-~11:10 PM.

railStations.name: Budapest Nyugati
railStations.note: The Western station with Eiffel-designed hall: trains to Szeged, Debrecen, Romania and northern Hungary. Metro M3 underneath, trams 4/6 outside.
railStations.hours: Station open ~4 AM-~midnight; M3 ~4:30 AM-~11:10 PM.

airports.name: Budapest Liszt Ferenc Airport
airports.transitNote: The 100E express bus runs direct to Kálvin tér, Astoria and Deák Ferenc tér in ~40 min on a dedicated airport ticket (~HUF 2,500). Cheaper: bus 200E to Kőbánya-Kispest, then metro M3 (on this map) to the centre; ordinary BKK tickets apply. Taxis ~HUF 12,000-15,000. The bus links are not on the metro map.
airports.hours: 100E runs day and night (every ~15-30 min); 200E ~4 AM-~11 PM; M3 ~4:30 AM-~11:10 PM.
